Definition: middle voice from G1909 and G2983; to seize (for help, injury, attainment, or any other purpose; literally or figuratively):--catch, lay hold (up-)on, take (by, hold of, on).
BiblicalUsage: Epilambanomai means to take hold of, to seize — for help, for rescue, for attainment. Jesus immediately stretched forth His hand and caught Peter sinking; He took a child and set him by Him; Barnabas took Paul and brought him to the apostles; He took on Him the seed of Abraham; and we are told to lay hold on eternal life.
TheologicalSignificance: Christ takes hold of the sinking, the child, and the seed of Abraham, and then tells us to take hold of eternal life the same way. I hold that the gospel is a taking hold, and the hand that caught Peter is the hand that holds me.
